title: Let your coding agents message each other for help
summary: A developer built agentsocks so Claude Code and Codex sessions can ask each other questions and hand off tasks; they use it to plan, build and review features.
agent_role: Claude plans and coordinates, Codex writes the code, another model reviews and sends findings back; the human decides what ships.
outcome: Author reports Codex asked another agent to sharpen a tagline and got the answer back automatically.
what_they_did: A developer built a free tool that lets one coding agent session message another. Claude plans a feature and hands work to Codex. A different model reviews the changes and sends findings straight back. Stuck agents ask another model to challenge their diagnosis.
how_it_went: The author says it removes the need to relay messages by hand, and shows Codex getting a tagline improved by another agent. They still decide what ships.
worth_knowing: Group channels and asking up to 16 sessions at once are labelled experimental. It runs on one machine by default.
prompt: Using a tool that lets my coding agent sessions message each other, plan the feature [feature description] for [repo]. Hand the coding work to my second agent session as a tracked task. When it finishes, send the changes to a third session for review and route its findings back to the builder. If anyone gets stuck on a bug, ask another session to challenge the diagnosis first. Show me the final changes and wait for my approval before committing or merging.

curation.rationale: Mostly a tool launch, but it describes a real workflow where one agent plans, another builds and a third reviews, with messages passed automatically; results are lightly evidenced.
